transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Martinez (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (ClearPath Eng Mgr), Daniel Kim (ClearPath ML Eng), Marta Lopez (ClearPath CTO)
Shared artifacts: https://docs.redwood.ai/migration-parity (parity mapping), https://redwood.ai/console-demo (console screenshots)

Summary: quick demo showing API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together-style calls into the Redwood API + console walkthrough (routes, model pinning, Optimize suggestions). Discussed streaming, function calling differences, embeddings mapping, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and next steps for a POC.

[00:00] Evan: alright everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Evan from Redwood, this is Maya on the SE side, we'll run through how you'd map your existing OpenAI / Anthropic usage over to Redwood and show the Console and Optimize features that help with batching and quantization suggestions.
[00:12] Priya: thanks Evan, quick context — we're currently primarily on OpenAI for chat and embeddings, some inference goes to Together for a couple of private models. we have production latency targets of sub-200ms p50 for short prompts and cost is a big factor.
[00:25] Maya: got it. can you remind us of the main APIs you're using? completions, chat completions, embeddings, streaming?
[00:34] Daniel: mostly chat completions (gpt-4-ish for high value flows), embeddings for semantic search, a few streaming use cases for live agents. we're also exploring function calling but not in prod yet.
[00:45] Evan: perfect. the migration we'll show is two parts: 1) api parity — how do parameters like temperature, top_p, max_tokens, function calling map — and 2) runtime/ops — routing, model pinning, and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization to hit cost/latency targets.
[00:59] Marta: curious about Together — they use a slightly different tokenization and some of our prompts behave differently. how do you handle model output parity?
[01:10] Maya: good question. parity isn't perfect across model families — what we do is provide mapping guidance and model recommendation table: we propose equivalent Redwood-verified model variants and show expected delta in outputs. we also run a prompt-level A/B with your prompt set in the POC to quantify regressions. link to the parity sheet is in the notes.
[01:30] Priya: ok show us the API mapping. the biggest risk is breaking behavior with function calls and streaming.
[01:38] Evan: sure — opening the doc: on the left we've got the OpenAI call: POST /v1/chat/completions with messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens. on Redwood you can call POST /v1/responses or our /v1/chat endpoint depending on SDK — we have example curl and SDK snippets that mimic messages arrays. streaming is supported via chunked responses or websocket; function calling maps to our tools API — slight name diffs but payload is near-identical.
[02:08] Maya: (shares screen) here's a quick snippet: OpenAI style -> Redwood style. the keys map: messages -> messages, temperature the same, top_p same, max_tokens -> max_output_tokens, stop tokens -> stop. for embeddings, our endpoint accepts the embedding model names that equate to text-embedding-3-large etc.
[02:28] Daniel: so we need to search/replace max_tokens -> max_output_tokens across our codebase. any SDKs to help?
[02:33] Maya: yep our SDKs have a compatibility helper and we've published a migration guide. also we'll provide a small script you can run to diff requests during the POC.
[02:45] Priya: streaming — is latency better or worse on Redwood hosted vs running a dedicated pool?
[02:52] Evan: hosting depends on tier: hosted has fast cold-starts and generally good latency; Dedicated reserved capacity gives you more predictable throughput and lower tail latency since we avoid noisy neighbors. for sub-200ms p50 it's often easier with Dedicated or with hosted + regional routing to your cloud region.
[03:12] Marta: we need KMS and HSM for keys — does Redwood integrate with customer KMS?
[03:18] Maya: yes we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys in Private deployments; Dedicated also supports bring-your-own-key via KMS. audit logs and SOC2 controls are available — we'll send our security pack after the call.
[03:35] Daniel: how about rate limits — Together gave us some big bursts that caused throttling. does Redwood autoscale?
[03:42] Evan: autoscale for hosted and dedicated burst configs; you can also set per-route quotas and token limits. for migrations we recommend a staged rollout and using the Console's per-route dashboards to watch for errors and token spikes.
[03:58] Priya: walk us through the Console and Optimize recommendations.
[04:03] Maya: (screen) Console has Routes where you can pin a model for a route, add a rollout policy (canary weights), and set fallback model variants. Optimize is our cost/perf toolkit — it inspects invocation patterns and suggests batching window sizes, kv-cache prefixes to reuse, and quantization profiles. i have an example here: for chat with short prompts it suggests aggressive batching of 16 on GPUs and int8 quantized model for 95% cost savings estimate.
[04:38] Priya: aggressive batching — doesn't that increase latency?
[04:41] Maya: it does increase request latency slightly but reduces per-token cost. Optimize gives a cost/latency tradeoff curve and you can pick a point to match your SLOs. it also simulates the expected impact on p50/p95.
[04:56] Daniel: how do we do embeddings mapping? we use text-embedding-3-small on OpenAI.
[05:01] Maya: in the parity sheet we map their embeddings to our equivalent model names; we also include a recommended quantization profile for embedding-only workloads and caching suggestions for re-used inputs.
[05:15] Evan: practical demo: i'll show an example migration of a chat completion.
[05:20] Evan: (copies sample curl) OpenAI call: curl -X POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"gpt-4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize..."}],"temperature":0.2}'
[05:35] Evan: Redwood version: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"redwood-4-std","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize..."}],"temperature":0.2,"max_output_tokens":512}'
[05:55] Priya: ok looks straightforward. what about SDK call differences?
[06:00] Maya: our JavaScript SDK has a migrate helper that wraps OpenAI-structured args; for Python we have a shim. we'll give you those snippets.
[06:10] Marta: downstream logging — can we keep the same request IDs so tracing works with our APMS?
[06:15] Evan: yes we preserve request ids if you pass X-Request-ID; Console tracing integrates with your tracing via forwarding headers and trace links show up in the per-route traces.
[06:28] Daniel: function calling — will we have to rewrite tool definitions?
[06:31] Maya: tool shapes are the same but nomenclature is slightly different. Redwood expects tools as part of the tools array and returns a 'tool_call' object; it's essentially one-to-one but we include example conversions in the parity sheet. occasional field name mismatches happen (e.g., 'name' vs 'tool_name') — small diffs.
[06:52] Priya: can you walk through a canary rollout? we want to test 5% of traffic to Redwood and fallback to OpenAI if errors spike.
[06:58] Maya: Console -> Routes -> Create Route; you set primary model binding to redwood-4, and add fallback to openai-gpt4 with a rule: if error_rate > 2% then route 100% to fallback. weight-based rollouts allow 5% to redwood initially. We also have automated rollback if latency or error thresholds breach.
[07:25] Daniel: benchmarking — do you provide a harness?
[07:28] Evan: yes, we'll share a harness that replays your prompt set with timing and token measurement; Maya will prepare it with instructions.
[07:36] Marta: on cost — what's typical delta vs OpenAI?
[07:39] Evan: depends a lot on model choice and quantization. for many embedding-heavy workloads we see 30-60% lower cost with similar quality using Redwood-verified models + Optimize recommendations; for chat it varies — the POC will give concrete numbers.
[07:56] Priya: are there cases where outputs differ and we should expect to re-work prompts?
[08:00] Maya: yes, especially switching model families (Anthropic -> Redwood). parity table highlights prompts likely to regress; our evals include sample outputs and recommended prompt nudges.
[08:12] Daniel: integration with SSO and RBAC — do you provide fine grained roles?
[08:16] Evan: yes RBAC with roles (viewer, operator, admin) and SSO via SAML/OIDC. we'll include a quickstart for SSO in the security pack.
[08:29] Priya: ok let's do a short deep dive on streaming — we have a live agent UI and need low tail latency.
[08:34] Maya: streaming options: 1) chunked HTTP streaming that sends partial deltas every 100-200ms, 2) websocket-based stream for bi-directional, 3) server-sent events. for low tail latency, KV cache reuse and keeping the model's context small helps. we also recommend model variants tuned for fast generation.
[09:00] Daniel: KV cache — any special config needed when migrating?
[09:04] Maya: if you use long-running chats you can persist kv-cache using our cache APIs; Optimize suggests prefix strategies to reuse keys across similar sessions. sometimes tokenization differences mean you need to align session boundaries.
[09:22] Evan: addressing Marta's Together question: for models that are open-source family we often recommend a Redwood-verified quantized checkpoint that preserves tokenization behavior; for closed models we recommend an equivalent model family and then do per-prompt eval.
[09:40] Priya: show me the Optimize console with a sample recommendation for batching.
[09:45] Maya: (shares screen) here's an Optimize run: it scanned traces and suggested batch_size: 16 for 80 tokens average, and quantization profile int8 with a projected cost reduction. you can accept suggestions which will populate a deployable config that your infra team can review.
[10:05] Daniel: if we accept those configs, can we test them in canary without changing code?
[10:09] Maya: yes, Console supports override configs per-route; you can enable batching at the routing layer so no code change needed — it's applied at the inference layer.
[10:18] Priya: networking & VPC — for Private deployment do you require us to open inbound?
[10:22] Evan: Private offers a couple of topologies: in VPC mode we peer networks and talk over private links; for on-prem air-gapped we ship an appliance. we'll have your infra team review the topology doc.
[10:36] Marta: security review will need SOC2 artifacts and a subprocessor list.
[10:40] Evan: yes will send security pack; we have SOC2 Type II and ISO documents, and the subprocessor list.
[10:48] Daniel: any known gotchas with embeddings dimension differences? some libraries assume 1536 dims.
[10:52] Maya: we map to equivalent dims; sometimes dims differ (e.g., 1536 vs 1024) — Optimize suggests remapping or reindexing strategies. for semantic search we recommend reindexing during the migration window.
[11:06] Priya: what about telemetry retention for debugging?
[11:09] Evan: Console stores traces and token-level logs configurable by retention. enterprise customers can increase retention in dedicated/private.
[11:18] Maya: quick note on model updates: you can pin model versions or opt into auto-updates; for prod we suggest pinning during POC to avoid drift.
[11:30] Evan: ok i'm going to show a quick end-to-end user flow: create route, pin model, set 5% rollout, enable fallback, run a simple sample traffic.
[11:38] Evan: (screen) create route -> name: chat-support -> primary: redwood-4-std -> fallback: openai-gpt4 -> rollout: 5% weight -> conditions: error_rate > 2% -> auto-rollback true. then run a test script which hits the route.
[12:05] Daniel: nice. will the request IDs stitch to our APM?
[12:09] Maya: yes if you forward trace headers we show links to your APM.
[12:17] Priya: if responses are slightly different for high-stakes prompts, can we keep OpenAI for those while moving everything else?
[12:22] Evan: absolutely. route-level pinning and per-prompt routing allows that granularity. common pattern: keep 10% traffic on original provider for high-sensitivity paths.
[12:35] Marta: for cost modelling, can you run a cost estimate for our current monthly token usage?
[12:40] Evan: we can — we'll need your usage snapshot; post-call I'll run an estimate and include it in the parity sheet.
[12:51] Priya: any difference in embedding nearest-neighbor performance?
[12:55] Maya: embeddings quality is model-dependent; we evaluate recall/precision on your sample set during POC. often quality is comparable, sometimes better depending on model.
[13:09] Daniel: talk me through error handling and retries.
[13:13] Maya: Console has retry policies and idempotency keys; we also expose client-side guidance for exponential backoff. fallback routes help reduce hard failures.
[13:25] Evan: ok next i'm going to show a code example for function calling conversion.
[13:30] Evan: (reads) OpenAI: functions: [{"name":"get_order","parameters":{...}}] Redwood: tools: [{"tool_name":"get_order","schema":{...}}] response includes 'tool_call' and we provide a small shim that adapts the response.
[13:48] Daniel: small diffs but manageable.
[13:51] Priya: what's the timeline you'd recommend for a POC?
[13:55] Evan: typical POC is 2-3 weeks: week 1 instrumentation and baseline measurements, week 2 run candidate models + Optimize suggestions, week 3 finalize config and run A/B. we can compress if you have smaller prompt set.
[14:12] Marta: any compliance for EU data residency?
[14:16] Maya: yes we have EU regions and data residency options on Dedicated/Private. hosted also allows region selection.
[14:24] Daniel: let's talk about a quick pilot: we want to test chat-support route (low risk) with 5% traffic. can you help setup?
[14:31] Evan: yes Maya will own the setup with you. she'll need API keys and a sample traffic replay.
[14:38] Maya: i'll follow up with a checklist and the benchmark harness.
[14:42] Priya: excellent. anything else re: vendor lock-in?
[14:47] Evan: we design the platform to be API-first and recommend keeping provider-agnostic wrappers in your code so swapping providers is easier; Console's route layer enables provider-level toggles without code changes.
[15:00] Marta: on the team side who should we loop in for security sign-off?
[15:04] Evan: send us a list; our security team will schedule a SOC2 walkthrough.
[15:12] Daniel: quick question — Together has slightly different tokenization for some punctuation which caused hallucination differences; do you offer tokenization tooling?
[15:20] Maya: yes we include tokenizers and a tokenization diff tool to show where boundaries change and suggest prompt edits.
[15:33] Priya: okay let's recap next steps.
[15:36] Evan: recap: 1) Evan to send parity mapping spreadsheet + cost estimate; 2) Maya to send benchmark harness and schedule POC next week; 3) Customer to share prompt set, SSO/SAML details, and current usage snapshot.
[15:49] Marta: agreed. pair on dates offline.
[15:52] Daniel: one last thing, function calling with structured json — any data masking?
[15:56] Maya: Console offers redaction filters and we can configure token-level redaction for sensitive fields during logging.
[16:05] Priya: great. thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-heard brand names and minor punctuation errors. speakers sometimes overlap; speaker labels are best-effort.
